module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 34

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 34](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$\operatorname{path}(G) \ge \lceil \operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(C, V)
+ \operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V) \rceil$,
where $\operatorname{path}(G)$ is the number of vertices of a largest induced path of $G$,
$C$ is the set of center vertices (those with minimum eccentricity), $M$ is the set of
maximum-degree vertices, and $\operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(S, V)$ is the average
of all nonzero distances $\operatorname{dist}\_G(s, v)$ with $s \in S$ and $v \in V$.

The conjecture is false. Let $G$ be the tree on $39$ vertices formed by a vertex with three
pendant leaves, joined by a path of five edges to the root of a perfect binary tree of depth
four. Then $\operatorname{path}(G) = 11$, while $C$ and $M$ are singletons whose distance sums
are $154$ and $266$, so the bound is $\lceil (154 + 266) / 38 \rceil = 12$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture34 :
  answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
      let C : Set α := center G
      let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
      let distAvg (S : Set α) : ℝ :=
        open scoped Classical in
        let pairs := (S.toFinset ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter (fun p => G.dist p.1 p.2 ≠ 0)
        (∑ p ∈ pairs, (G.dist p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / pairs.card
      Int.ceil (distAvg C + distAvg M) ≤ (path G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `path G` invariant is nonneg when cast to ℤ. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

/-- The edgeless graph on 3 vertices has no edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).edgeFinset.card = 0 := by simp

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly assumes Nontrivial α, whereas the source says only “simple connected graph.”
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This restriction does not change the universal claim with the file's totalized average formula. Dropping Nontrivial adds only singleton connected graphs: every distance is zero, both filtered averages are zero, and the inequality is automatic. Empty graphs are not Connected. The scratch file proves the equivalence of the universally quantified statements with and without Nontrivial; wrapping these equivalent propositions in answer(False) ↔ preserves equivalence.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 34 and surrounding remarks: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161837id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html

review.notes:
No mathematical defects found in the main theorem or either sanity check. The source explicitly defines path as the number of vertices of a largest induced path and both distance averages using all nonzero distances, exactly as formalized. Connectedness prevents unreachable-distance default values, and the two averaging denominators are positive under the hypotheses.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and checks boundary cases and the documented counterexample independently of conjecture34. Lean checks establish that the 39-vertex graph is a tree, identify its singleton center and maximum-degree sets, and verify distance sums 154 and 266 and ceiling 12. Its diameter is 10, so its largest induced path has 11 vertices, validating answer(False).

The live cited host timed out, so archived primary pages were used. The archived list retains an open label and reports a last update in 2020. Given the valid explicit counterexample, this does not warrant changing the file's solved status or negative answer.
